These instructions guide GitHub Copilot in the BudgetWise project. ASP.NET Core Web API (.NET 8) + React TypeScript frontend (Vite, Tailwind CSS). Training app for Copilot Workshop.

Follow standard C# naming conventions (PascalCase for classes/methods/properties, camelCase for local variables/parameters); meaningful/descriptive names; methods focused/concise (single responsibility); Prefer composition over inheritance; Use C# 12 features where appropriate (primary constructors, collection expressions, etc.); Use `var` for locals when type is obvious; Place `using` statements inside namespace declarations. Use TypeScript for all new code with strict type checking; React best practices (hooks, functional components); components focused/reusable; Tailwind utility classes (no inline styles); semantic HTML; accessibility (ARIA, keyboard); dependency injection via constructor parameters; proper service lifetimes (Scoped/Singleton/Transient). Use minimal API endpoints or controller-based consistently; RESTful naming: nouns + HTTP methods; return `IActionResult` or typed results (`Ok<T>`, `NotFound`) from controller actions. Use model validation (Data Annotations); separate DTOs for request/response; `record` for immutable DTOs; Data Annotations (e.g., `[Required]`, `[MaxLength]`); explicit mapping domain↔DTO; XML docs on all public classes/methods with `<summary>`, `<param>`, `<returns>`, `<exception>`; comments explain WHY, not just WHAT; `// TODO:` marks incomplete features with clear description; when implementing TODO, follow existing patterns; update documentation when adding features. Prioritize clarity; beginner-friendly; add comments for .NET Core/React concepts.

Testing: .NET xUnit; frontend React Testing Library; AAA (Arrange/Act/Assert); method names `MethodName_WhenCondition_ThenExpectedResult`; integration: `WebApplicationFactory<T>`; unit: mock external deps; test success/failure/edge/boundary; test user interactions; use `screen` queries; mock API calls with M
